A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text and Appendices A–E. Equations, experiments, figures, and tables can be matched, including relocated and merged material.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic linear-regression experiments, including learned attention weights, training dynamics, prediction losses, activation ablations, and multitask experiments in Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in the main text and Appendix A.

M1.justification: The single-layer multi-head attention architecture, inputs, prediction readout, training objective, and learned-predictor formulation are retained. Expository and notation edits do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic regression with isotropic and correlated Gaussian covariates, overlapping multitask signals, and varying test-sequence lengths. Renaming non-isotropic covariates as anisotropic does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Figures 4, 8, and 11 retain the same attention-model comparisons and vanilla GD, debiased GD, and ridge/Bayes estimators. The newly cited related works are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Data generation, model configurations, MSE evaluation, training budgets, and length-generalization procedures are retained. Table 1 re-expresses parameter magnitudes using the first head of the opposing two-head pair; no changed experimental procedure is documented.

E4.justification: The activation ablations, head-count and dummy-head analyses, covariance analysis, multitask superposition examples, and loss-approximation validations are retained. Combining existing displays in Figure 19 adds no analysis.

E5.justification: Both retain qualitative references to repeated runs and different random seeds in Section 5.4 and Appendix A.1. There are no added run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or changed uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: The plotted results and numerical tables are retained. For example, Table 1's exponential-activation values remain 0.1267, 3.5006, and 0.8871. All parameter values from v1's Table 2 reappear transposed within v2's Figure 19.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 removes a short intermediate Taylor-expansion derivation connecting loss terms to the sign-matching and zero-sum gradient components. This reduces documented derivation detail; the resulting updates, Proposition 4.1, Theorem 4.2, and substantive appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about emergent attention patterns, debiased GD, multi-head advantages, length generalization, and anisotropic and multitask extensions.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 expands the existing edge-of-stability interpretation by describing nonmonotonic gradient descent oscillating between valley walls and failing to converge fully. The principal applicability qualifications and limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The code-access footnote changes the repository location from XintianPan/ICL_linear to Y-Agent/ICL_linear. Training and hardware disclosures remain. Appendix A.2 removes a duplicated setup paragraph whose settings remain documented in Sections 3 and 5.3.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 adds a substantial comparison with Chen et al. (2024a) and newly cited Cui et al. (2024), distinguishing initialization, head allocation, learned predictors, and theoretical approaches. Aksenov et al. (2024) and Sun et al. (2025) are also added, materially expanding research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes local prose edits, promotes the two training stages to numbered subsections, revises appendix headings, and changes terminology and affiliation presentation. The overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v1's Table 2 is transposed and combined with the existing heatmaps in Figure 19. Other figures are resized or repositioned, and table rules, highlighted boxes, and captions receive limited formatting changes.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparison with closely related studies makes the contribution easier to assess, while numbered training stages and the combined Figure 19 improve navigation and comparison. These modest benefits outweigh the shortened derivation and small editorial regressions, including the new 'Table 19' reference. Experimental evidence and central theoretical results remain unchanged.
